title: Ownership, Borrowing, Slices, and Collections
summary: Apply moves, copies, shared and mutable borrows, lifetimes, slices, String, Vec, and HashMap without invalid references.

Use compiler, lint, and test evidence to verify behavior

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Each Rust value has an owner and is dropped when that owner leaves scope. Assignment of a non-Copy value usually moves ownership, preventing accidental double use. A shared reference `&T` permits reading; an exclusive reference `&mut T` permits mutation, and their active use cannot conflict. References must never outlive the data they borrow. Slices borrow contiguous regions without ownership. `Vec<T>` owns a growable sequence, but pushing may reallocate and invalidate element references, so keep borrows short. HashMap lookup returns an Option.
keyPoints: Each Rust value has an owner and is dropped when that owner leaves scope.
commonMistakes: off-by-one assumptions can skip or overrun values
building a chain alone may perform no work

sections.content:
1. Add the example to a Cargo project.
2. Predict types and ownership.
3. Run fmt, check, Clippy, and tests.
4. Fix one cause at a time.
5. Run the binary.
6. Add boundary tests.
